scope: pending_articles_repo.py (init_schema ALTER hold_reason, list_pending/count_pending/list_pending_stale/list_notified_overdue/list_pending_for_eviction/list_held/clear_hold), news_bot.py (_content_gate_subject/_hold_for_review_reason/_is_rejected_genre detectors, job() content-gate wiring, hd:<a|r>:<token> grammar + resolve_hold_callback + dispatch), admin_alerts.py ([E036]/[E037] builders + held-backlog line)
summary: The feature is well-built and mostly reuses the already-hardened promo-filter machinery correctly: the three new detectors (_hold_for_review_reason, _is_rejected_genre, _content_gate_subject) coerce every scanned field through _promo_scan_input/_promo_fold, never raise on non-str link/title/entry/article (verified with ~24 direct repros: list/dict/int/float/bool/bytes link, list/dict/int/float/bool/None title, None/str/list entry or article, malformed IPv6 URL, zero-width-split marker) and are additionally wrapped fail-open at the job() call site with dedicated tests (test_hold_detector_crash_is_fail_open, test_genre_detector_crash_is_fail_open, both re-run and passing). The one new regex (_GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_RE, anchored '^\s*watch\s*[:\-\u2013\u2014]') is linear, not vulnerable to ReDoS, and — like title/URL — is only ever evaluated on text already bounded to 2000 chars by _promo_scan_input (measured: a marker placed past the 2000-char boundary is not detected; 10MB title+link processes in ~0.2ms through both detectors). [E036]/[E037] reuse send_admin_notification verbatim (plain text, _redact_text, best-effort try/except) and truncate the untrusted title via the existing 200-char _PROMO_TITLE_MAXLEN cap; matched markers embedded in the alert are always our own constants, never raw attacker text. Legacy-row / idempotent-ALTER behaviour under normal conditions is correct and was verified directly: existing rows get NULL (publishable) for free, a restart mid-migration is safe (each ALTER is independently caught), and a concurrent writer holding the table for ~0.8s (under the 5s busy_timeout) is waited out cleanly with no error and no data loss. However two real, reproducible issues were found that were not covered by the existing test suite. HIGH: the idempotent-ALTER loop's `except sqlite3.OperationalError: pass` is not scoped to 'duplicate column name' — when a concurrent writer holds the table PAST the 5s busy_timeout, the ALTER raises 'database is locked' (also an OperationalError) and this is silently swallowed exactly like an already-migrated column; init_db() returns as if nothing happened, hold_reason is genuinely absent, and the very next call to list_pending/count_pending/insert_pending (core, always-invoked-every-tick queries, unlike the softer-touch model_fingerprint/telegraph_url columns this pattern was previously used for) will then raise 'no such column: hold_reason' uncaught — crash-looping job() on every subsequent tick/restart with zero log line pointing at the real cause. Reproduced empirically with a real threading contention test (writer holds an IMMEDIATE lock >5s; init_db() returns cleanly in ~5.1s with exception=None; hold_reason confirmed still missing afterward). This is a pre-existing pattern shared with three earlier migrations (not introduced by this diff), but this diff is what puts a column behind that fragile idempotency check onto the hot path that gates all publishing. MEDIUM: the hd:/dd: token store (pending_articles_repo.bot_state key 'review_token:<token>' -> link) has no grammar/kind scoping — put_review_token/get_review_token_link/delete_review_token are a single flat namespace shared by both features, and dispatch in _handle_review_update is purely by action-word membership, never by which resolver actually minted the token. Reproduced two concrete cross-grammar outcomes: (1) a token minted by the E014 (dd:) send site for an ordinary non-held pending row, redeemed via resolve_hold_callback('reject', token, admin) as if the wire had been 'hd:r:<token>', silently DELETES that ordinary article (skip_pending) even though it was never held — resolve_hold_callback's reject branch uses the unfiltered get_pending, not scoped to hold_reason; (2) a token minted by the new E036 (hd:) send site for a genuinely HELD row, redeemed via resolve_dedup_callback('keep', token, admin) as if the wire had been 'dd:k:<token>', answers '👍 Оставлено' and deletes the token as a terminal outcome while leaving hold_reason untouched — the article is now PERMANENTLY held with no live button/token anywhere to release it (matches the documented 'no re-mint utility' limitation, i.e. no recovery path). Both directly contradict the code's own stated invariant ('a shared prefix would route a press into the wrong resolver, which would answer «ustarela» and lose the decision') — my repros show the wrong resolver's REAL action fires instead of a safe stale-token no-op. Mitigating factor: _is_admin_press still runs first in both paths (verified: a non-admin press touches zero pending_repo functions and returns (None, "")), so this requires the already-authenticated single-admin Telegram context to trigger and is not reachable by tapping a real rendered button (Telegram always echoes back exactly the embedded callback_data) — it is a defense-in-depth / blast-radius gap, not a privilege-escalation path for an outside party. TestReviewCallbackGrammarsCoexist covers cross-grammar LETTER rejection at the parser and same-grammar routing, but does not cover cross-grammar TOKEN reuse, so this gap is genuinely untested. LOW/INFO: the held backlog ('На утверждении: N') has no threshold/escalation alarm unlike count_pending's >50 warning — a misbehaving (not malicious; SOURCES is a fixed operator-configured list per the already-accepted SEC-PROMO-5 precedent) source that puts a HOLD marker in many distinct titles could grow an invisible-to-count_pending backlog with only a slowly-incrementing number in the daily ping. This is a documented, operator-approved decision (SESSION-2026-07-25.md «Чего сознательно НЕ делаем» #4) and is bounded per-URL (the link PK + pre-b3 get_pending filter prevent the same article from re-inflating the backlog), so it is recorded informationally only, matching the prior audit's own precedent — not a blocker. All 1520 tests + 187 subtests pass in a clean, isolated worktree at 98cadd7 (note: the shared working directory had unrelated concurrent in-progress edits from another process during this review, which produced spurious full-suite flakiness on that copy; testing was redirected to an isolated `git worktree add --detach` checkout of 98cadd7 to get a trustworthy signal, and results below are all from that clean checkout).

findings.area: prod DB migration safety / availability (silent-fail then crash-loop)
findings.location: pending_articles_repo.py init_schema(), lines ~236-244 — the ADD COLUMN loop's `except sqlite3.OperationalError: pass`; consumed every tick via news_bot.job() -> init_db() (news_bot.py:3331) and at startup via main() -> init_db() (news_bot.py:4140)
findings.description: The idempotent-migration pattern (reused unchanged from the telegraph_url/model_fingerprint precedents, now applied to `pending_articles.hold_reason` too) catches `sqlite3.OperationalError` broadly and treats ANY instance as 'column already exists'. sqlite3 raises the SAME exception class for 'database is locked' (when the busy_timeout, 5.0s by Python's own sqlite3.connect default, is exceeded by a concurrent writer) and for other operational failures (readonly filesystem, disk I/O error). All of these are silently swallowed exactly like a genuine already-migrated no-op — no log line, no admin alert, no retry.
findings.reproduction: Built a real threading repro: stripped hold_reason back out of a temp DB (simulating a not-yet-migrated legacy prod DB), spawned a writer thread holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` + a write for >5s (past the 5.0s busy_timeout `sqlite3.connect(DB_FILE)` uses by Python default inside news_bot.init_db()), then called `news_bot.init_db()` from the main thread concurrently. Result: init_db() returned normally after ~5.13s with `exception=None` (i.e. no exception escaped, migration 'succeeded' from the caller's point of view), but `PRAGMA table_info(pending_articles)` afterward confirms `hold_reason` is genuinely ABSENT. Separately confirmed the two error messages are distinguishable in this sqlite3 build ('duplicate column name: hold_reason' vs 'database is locked'), so a scoped catch is straightforward.
findings.impact: list_pending(), count_pending(), list_pending_stale(), list_notified_overdue() and list_pending_for_eviction() all now unconditionally reference `hold_reason IS NULL` in their WHERE clause, and insert_pending() unconditionally inserts into the hold_reason column — none of these have a try/except around their `conn.execute(...)` call. On a DB where the ALTER silently failed as above, the VERY NEXT call to any of them raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: hold_reason` uncaught. Per the SEC-PROMO-1 precedent (already accepted for this codebase's threat model), job() has no top-level try/except around this section and job() itself is invoked with no wrapper (immediate call + `schedule.every().day.at(...).do(job)` inside a bare `while True` loop) — so this crashes the daemon process. Because list_pending/count_pending run every tick (not just once at startup) and the crash happens BEFORE mark_processed for whatever entry triggered it, and because init_db() re-attempts the SAME broad-except ALTER on every subsequent job()/main() call, the failure mode is a genuine crash-loop that silently blocks ALL publishing (not just content-gate) until an operator manually inspects the DB schema — with no error message anywhere pointing at 'hold_reason is missing' as the cause. This is the exact failure class (uncaught exception in an always-on hot path, crash before mark_processed, no operator signal) that the project's own 'a filter must never block publishing' contract (Decision 12/AC9) and the SEC-PROMO-1 finding were written to close, but reached via the migration path rather than a detector.
findings.recommendation: Scope the except to the specific, expected case instead of any OperationalError, e.g. `except sqlite3.OperationalError as e: if 'duplicate column' not in str(e).lower(): raise` (or log+re-raise / alert on the else branch), OR switch to a check-before-ALTER pattern (`PRAGMA table_info(pending_articles)` and only ALTER if the column is absent) which sidesteps exception-based idempotency entirely and lets a genuine lock/I-O failure propagate and be seen. Either fix should ship before/alongside this migration, since prod restarts and daily ticks will keep re-running this exact ALTER against a live, concurrently-written database.

findings.location: pending_articles_repo.py put_review_token/get_review_token_link/delete_review_token (lines ~1213-1259, single flat `review_token:<token>` -> link namespace in bot_state, shared by both grammars); news_bot.py resolve_hold_callback (reject branch uses unfiltered get_pending), resolve_dedup_callback (keep branch deletes the token without checking hold_reason), _handle_review_update dispatch (news_bot.py:918-929, dispatches purely on action-word membership, never checks which grammar actually minted the token)
findings.description: The [E014] dd: and [E036] hd: grammars share ONE token->link store with no field recording which grammar/feature minted a given token. Both resolvers trust `pending_repo.get_review_token_link(token)` unconditionally and act on whatever link comes back using their own action semantics, regardless of whether that token was actually minted by their own send site. The code's own docstring on `_REVIEW_CALLBACK_GRAMMARS` claims 'a shared [prefix] would route a press into the wrong resolver, which would answer «ustarela» and lose the decision' — implying cross-grammar attempts safely no-op — but that guarantee only covers the PARSER's letter-validity check (verified correct: 'dd:a:', 'hd:c:' etc. are rejected), not token provenance, which is not checked anywhere.
findings.reproduction: Two independent repros against a real temp DB: (1) staged an ordinary non-held pending row, minted a token for it via `put_review_token` (the same call the E014 dd: send site makes), then called `news_bot.resolve_hold_callback('reject', token, admin_id)` (as if the wire were 'hd:r:<token>' instead of the real 'dd:c:'/'dd:k:' that would have been rendered) — result: status '🚨 Не будет опубликовано', and the row is confirmed DELETED from pending_articles (get_pending returns None, list_pending no longer contains it) even though it was never a held/content-gate row. (2) staged a held (hold_reason='poster') row, minted its token the way the new hd: send site does, then called `news_bot.resolve_dedup_callback('keep', token, admin_id)` (as if the wire were 'dd:k:<token>') — result: status '👍 Оставлено', hold_reason confirmed UNCHANGED ('poster', still held) but `get_review_token_link(token)` confirmed None afterward — the token was consumed as a terminal outcome with no state change to the hold, permanently orphaning the article (no other token/button exists for it, and per the feature's own documented scope there is no re-mint/un-hold utility).
findings.impact: Both outcomes require the callback to already pass `_is_admin_press` (verified separately: a non-admin press calls zero pending_repo functions and returns (None, ""), so this is NOT reachable by an unauthenticated or non-admin party) and are not reachable via normal button-tapping (a real inline keyboard press always echoes back exactly the callback_data embedded at build time, and build_hold_review_keyboard/the dedup keyboard builder never mix prefixes). Realistic triggers are limited to the admin's own compromised/scripted Telegram context, a stray/replayed callback, or a future third grammar reusing put_review_token/get_review_token_link without awareness of the shared namespace. Given that, this is a defense-in-depth and blast-radius gap rather than a privilege-escalation vulnerability — but the concrete consequences are real and silent: an ordinary pending article can be deleted without ever having been held, and a held article can be permanently and silently locked with no recovery path other than manual DB surgery, both without any error surfaced to the operator. TestReviewCallbackGrammarsCoexist (the test class added specifically for this diff) covers parser-level cross-grammar letter rejection and same-grammar routing, but does not cover cross-grammar TOKEN reuse, so this is a genuine, currently-untested gap.
findings.recommendation: Scope tokens to their grammar, e.g. store the bot_state key as `review_token:<grammar>:<token>` (grammar = 'dd'/'hd') and have each resolver look up only its own namespace (get_review_token_link(token, grammar='hd') style), or store a `kind` alongside `link` in put_review_token and have resolve_hold_callback / resolve_dedup_callback each verify `kind` matches before acting, falling back to the existing safe '⚠️ Кнопка устарела' outcome on a mismatch (which is what the docstring already claims happens). Add a regression test that mints a token via one grammar's real send path and asserts the OTHER resolver treats it as unknown/stale rather than acting on it.

findings.description: Unlike `count_pending()`'s existing `> 50` backlog warning, the held-backlog line ('На утверждении: N') has no threshold or escalation — it is a plain always-rendered count with no alarm regardless of how large N grows.
findings.impact: A source that repeatedly publishes DISTINCT URLs whose titles contain a HOLD marker (e.g. 'poster', 'catalog') would silently grow the held backlog with only a slowly-incrementing number in the daily ping and no alarm, while never buying an extra publish slot or triggering the existing backlog alarm (both intentionally excluded, per design). This is explicitly a DOCUMENTED, operator-approved decision recorded in work/SESSION-2026-07-25.md ('Чего сознательно НЕ делаем' item 4: 'no operator way to browse/drain the HOLD backlog ... if the backlog starts accumulating, we'll revisit'), and matches the already-accepted SEC-PROMO-5 rationale: SOURCES is a fixed, operator-configured list of feeds/scrapers rather than open third-party submission, so this is a misbehaving-source risk, not an attacker-controlled one. It is also bounded per-URL: the `link` PK plus the pre-b3 `get_pending` filter (which deliberately sees held rows) prevent the same article from being re-staged and re-inflating the backlog on subsequent ticks.
findings.recommendation: No change required to merge — matches an already-accepted precedent and a decision the operator explicitly made with eyes open. If the held backlog is observed to grow in practice, add a threshold line (e.g. 'На утверждении: N (!)' past some N) mirroring the existing `> 50` pattern, and/or the deferred 'show all held' operator command noted as future work.

checks_performed: Read the full commit 98cadd7 diff (git show) across pending_articles_repo.py, news_bot.py, admin_alerts.py and their tests; read work/SESSION-2026-07-25.md Content-gate section end-to-end; read both prior promo-filter-review/security-auditor*.json reports to avoid re-litigating already-accepted items (SEC-PROMO-3 evasion, SEC-PROMO-5 false-positive permanence, unbounded link-length in alerts) which this diff inherits unchanged.

Discovered the live working directory had unrelated, in-progress uncommitted edits from a concurrent process (a further video-marker refinement) during this review; redirected all test execution to an isolated `git worktree add --detach <path> 98cadd7` checkout to get a trustworthy, uncontaminated signal, after the contaminated copy produced non-reproducible full-suite failures that vanished once isolated.

Ran the full test suite 3x in the isolated worktree: 1520 passed, 187 subtests passed, consistently, in ~21-24s each run (vs ~50-100s+ and sporadic failures on the contaminated shared copy, confirming the contamination theory).

Directly called _hold_for_review_reason / _is_rejected_genre with ~24 malformed-input shapes (non-str link as list/dict/int/float/bool/bytes, non-str title as list/dict/int/float/bool/None, entry=None/str/int, article=None/list/str, malformed IPv6 URL, zero-width-space-split marker) — zero exceptions, all degrade to safe empty/partial results.

Timed _GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_RE against adversarial padding/repetition inputs (microseconds, no backtracking blowup) and confirmed the 2000-char _promo_scan_input cap is enforced BEFORE both the lead-regex and the marker scan (a marker placed past the cap boundary in title or URL is not detected) and holds under 10MB title+link inputs (~0.2ms).

Ran the project's own fail-open regression tests (test_hold_detector_crash_is_fail_open, test_genre_detector_crash_is_fail_open) confirming a RuntimeError from either detector does not crash job() and the article is staged/published as usual, not silently parked.

Verified [E036]/[E037] both flow through the shared send_admin_notification (plain text / no parse_mode, _redact_text applied, best-effort try/except) — identical protection to the already-audited [E035] path; confirmed title truncation via the existing _PROMO_TITLE_MAXLEN=200 cap and that all rendered markers are drawn from fixed constant tuples, never raw attacker text (including the 'url:<marker>' slug-hit label).

Verified resolve_hold_callback calls _is_admin_press FIRST, before any pending_repo call, via a direct mock-call trace (patched get_review_token_link/clear_hold/skip_pending/delete_review_token, forced _is_admin_press False) — confirmed zero DB I/O and (None, "") return for a non-admin press, matching resolve_dedup_callback's established contract.

Verified _parse_review_callback_data correctly rejects every cross-grammar letter combination (dd:a:, dd:r:, hd:c:, hd:k:), unknown prefixes, empty fields, too-many-fields, and oversized (>64 byte) payloads, and that _REVIEW_CALLBACK_ACTIONS/_HOLD_ACTION_WORDS are disjoint (no shared action word), so dispatch-by-word in _handle_review_update cannot itself misroute a syntactically-correct callback.

Traced put_review_token/get_review_token_link/delete_review_token and confirmed they operate on one flat bot_state key namespace with no grammar/kind field, then reproduced two concrete cross-grammar-token-reuse outcomes end-to-end against a real SQLite DB (see SEC-CG-2) — a gap not covered by TestReviewCallbackGrammarsCoexist, which only tests parser-level letter rejection and same-grammar routing.

Verified migration idempotency and legacy-row semantics directly: init_schema's ALTER loop is safe to interrupt at any point (each statement independently caught) and existing rows get NULL (publishable) for free with no default value needed.

Reproduced the concurrent-writer + migration race under NORMAL conditions (writer holds lock ~0.8s, well under the 5s busy_timeout): init_db() blocks briefly and completes successfully, hold_reason added, concurrent write preserved, no error — confirming the happy path this feature's design doc claims.

Reproduced the SAME race PAST the 5s busy_timeout (see SEC-CG-1): confirmed the ALTER's exception is silently swallowed by the existing blanket `except sqlite3.OperationalError: pass`, hold_reason remains genuinely absent, and no error/log signals the failure.
Confirmed skip_pending() and clear_hold() are both fully parameterized (no string-built SQL) — no SQL injection surface from untrusted link/title/pub_date values anywhere in the new code.
Confirmed only one new regex exists in the entire diff (_GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_RE) via grep across the full news_bot.py diff hunks.

prod_migration_go_no_go: GO, with SEC-CG-1 queued as a prompt follow-up rather than a hard blocker. Under normal operating conditions (verified empirically) the `hold_reason` ALTER is safe: idempotent across restarts, existing rows correctly default to NULL/publishable, and a concurrent reviewer-listener writer holding the table for less than the 5s busy_timeout is waited out cleanly with no data loss. The one real gap (SEC-CG-1: a lock held PAST 5s during init_db() silently leaves the column missing, then crash-loops job() on every subsequent tick with no operator-visible cause) is a pre-existing pattern shared with three earlier, already-deployed migrations (telegraph_url/telegraph_path/model_fingerprint) that has evidently not manifested as a production incident so far — it is not new risk introduced by this diff's mechanics, only a new column riding an existing fragile idempotency check, now on a column referenced by the hottest, always-invoked queue queries. Recommend shipping the scoped-except (or check-before-ALTER) fix in a fast-follow commit before or shortly after this deploy, given the widened blast radius, but it does not need to block this migration going out.
